newsitem.title: GREECE: Weak industrials push Greek stocks below 1,600pts.
newsitem.headline: Weak industrials push Greek stocks below 1,600pts.

text.p: Greek equities came off their best towards the end of Tuesday's session, easing below 1,600 points with industrials, especially cement, being the weak spot of the bourse's blue chips.
Despite the fall, fund managers took a favourable view on the rise of the dollar in international markets.

"A stronger dollar favours export-oriented industries operating in the dollar area, such as cement, alumium and other metallurgical industries," said George Vlahakis, fund manager at European Reliance mutual funds.
The dollar eased from Monday's all time-high of 281.27 drachmas at the Bank of Greece's fixing to 281.02 on Tuesday.
"The effect on inflation via higher fuel and raw material prices is not worrisome because it has a limited, temporary effect," Vlahakis said.
The market was seen comfortably recovering the ground lost during recent price fluctuations with buying interest concentrating on high-growth blue chips.
The Athens general index softened 0.66 percent or 10.57 points to 1,590.33 from Monday's 1,600.90 close, trading narrowly between 1,589 and 1,606 points.
